reviews.comment: I think he really understand what's finance.

Teaches whatever you need on the tests however the class was 3 hours long and people tend to zone out after the first 1.5h. Tests are rather simple and open book and follow the same pattern as previous tests. Don't expect an A if you just cover previous papers.Replies to emails and answers some questions during the class.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Jansen's class covers applicable material but I have a hard time believing anyone retains it. Between super lengthy homework sets and massive tests that while they are open note, the first test was two hours and nobody was done by the time limit. Also can be mean for no reason if you ask him specifics about assignments etc.

McGrawHill homework takes about 2/3 hours each, look up the questions and rework them with your numbers to understand. Go over the previous exams and bring them on exam day, open note exams, typically the same questions with different numbers. This class is a lot of work, it is the same as 680, so if you want your master's save this class for that.
Class was made much more difficult than it should have been. Tests are barely doable in the time limit given.

Jansen is kind of a jerk for no reason and is often rude to students. For exams, just make an excel sheet answering all the homework questions- the exam questions were like 90% just homework questions with different numbers. His lectures and textbook are not relevant to tests. I literally got a 102 in this class and didn't learn a single thing.

By far the worst professor and hardest class I have taken in my life. I've never made below a B in my life and I managed to get a D in this class. The lectures and the book are extremely vague and in no way help on the homework and the tests. He is also horrible at responding to emails. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS

This class was fully asynchronous, and his videos weren't good at helping you on the homework. It's a pretty hard class but that being said, you can still do well in the class. He does a good class experiment that a free 100 and a portfolio project/memo that is also a free 100 and honestly fun to do. Not an amazing choice, but gets the job done.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures are verbatim from the textbook. The textbook is very surface level. The homeworks are the test questions. The textbook DOES NOT teach what you need to do the homework. Unless you have a Master's level understanding of Finance, do not take this class.

Dr. Jansen is a great professor and seems to genuinely enjoy helping students succeed. This is a hard class with tests (45%), group project (30%) and the rest being homework/participation. If you don't study the material this class is an uphill battle, but with a little effort an A is very attainable. Open note tests seemed to be graded generously.
